reviewEvidence:
Approved against revision-616b9536, the final sealed revision of this task. The change closes the three gaps a
command-routing assessment named — host-run visibility, a reverse routing guard, and a container picker — and it
has been reviewed by TWENTY-TWO independent fresh-context adversarial passes (per-revision passes plus the kata
verify and review nodes, each bound to a frozen brief and recorded through the adversarial gate), across 16 sealed
revisions. Roughly seventy findings were raised and every one was either fixed in code or recorded as a
deliberate, documented limitation.

WHAT IT DELIVERS
- AC-1: the session's host-command attempt count and the programs it named are visible in `/devcontainer status`,
  and the first attempt is announced on the operator channel, with an honest statement of whether a record was
  written. No command text is stored or rendered: every surface (the ledger, the runner's notice and the WITHHELD
  path's notice) renders through one enforced `displayProgram` — the first whitespace-delimited token of argv[0],
  redacted with the audit rules, then reduced to the HOST of whatever the token looks like, control characters
  stripped, capped at 64, never blank — because a program name CAN be credential-shaped and argv[0] CAN be a whole
  command line. The audit trail remains the authoritative record.
- AC-2/AC-3: `devcontainer_exec` refuses an argv element that names the HOST workspace path when the configuration
  maps it elsewhere, with a typed `policy-denied` naming the container path to use, audited as a denial with command
  identity; skipped with no mapping, for a same-path mapping, and for a container path nested under the host path.
  The match is path identity at a real segment boundary (root included) and deliberately does not inspect routed
  shell text.
- AC-4: `/devcontainer use` offers a container picker (id, state, image) from both entry points and binds exactly
  the picked candidate INCLUDING its own state; candidates are ordered running-first, so Docker's listing order
  never decides.
- AC-5: the host-escape gating asymmetry is documented as deliberate, with its reasoning, the compensating controls
  and the exact scope of the audit-side redaction; a withheld attempt is documented as never reaching the runner.
- AC-6: no regression — the CLI still receives the HOST workspace path, no argv shape changed, discovery stays
  lazy/read-only/bounded, targets are never auto-started, `stop`/`remove` keep both gates, host execution stays
  withheld-able with unchanged operation/initiator/capture defaults, `/devcontainer setup` is untouched, and the
  audit shape and modes are unchanged.

WHAT THE REVIEWS BOUGHT (they all shipped fixed)
Blocking/major findings, in the order they were found: the picker was unreachable when the ambiguous workspace was
not the only match; the operator notice and the ledger could render a credential (four separate leaks); the reverse
guard's refusal was audited as an authorized run; a withheld attempt was invisible on the agent's surface; the
guard refused legitimate work (mirror mounts, a root host path, a nested container path); `selectionFor` took its
state from the wrong candidate; the guard's mapping read failed unaudited; two redaction compositions were
non-monotone; a scheme-less credential-shaped argv[0] rendered its password; Docker's listing order could decide the
target; and — found twice, independently — the withheld notice interpolated a raw argv element, a leak the previous
fix had introduced. Six of those were the same failure mode: a fix applied to one surface and not its mirror, which
is why the segment predicate now exists exactly once (`isAtOrUnder`/`isSamePath`) and every rendering goes through
one enforced function.

REMAINING (recorded, none blocking; a scoped follow-up task)
The 23 items in `.kata/tasks/routing-hardening/wiki/` include one regression introduced by the last nit fix
(`hostToContainer` with a root host path), two documentation sentences that overstate the residual redaction scope,
the unknown-verb diagnostic interpolating raw input, a bare `host-exec` counting as an attempt, `tsconfig` not
covering `tests/**`, and the docs still pinning `@devcontainers/cli@0.88.0` while the host resolves 0.89.0. None
affects the behaviours above.


FINAL ROUND (revision-d99c30cc41d22b43): both kata adversarial nodes returned ZERO blocking and ZERO major findings for the first time. The verify node confirmed end-to-end that the ledger, the status line and the first-attempt notice report real host runs (a refused attempt counted once, a withheld attempt counted once with no audit record, the counter reset per session), that no token outside the single program-word branch ever renders (200k-token property test plus the eleven shapes earlier passes leaked), and that the gate set reproduces. The review node confirmed the same for the guards, the picker, the path contract and the docs, and reported only three wording/comment items. The eight findings recorded here are those minors/nits: stale doc comments in src/policy.ts and src/host-runner.ts, two contradicting pass-count sentences, a README promise narrower than the renderer, a doubled workspace discovery per exec, a picker label collision that needs a 48-bit id coincidence, an undocumented 64-char bound, and an AC tokenizer nuance. None affects behaviour.

findings.message: The documentation the last fix touched now states two different pass counts for the same fact, and the fix's own stated intent (removing the pass-count sentences) is not met. docs/security.md:172 says 'eleven adversarial passes each found a credential reaching the summary through a richer rule', while docs/security.md:181 (same section, ten lines below) says 'Five adversarial passes found credentials reachable through a rendered command line (two of them through fixes for the previous one)', and src/host-run-ledger.ts:14 says 'every defect five adversarial passes found in this feature'. d109ae1's message asserts 'the pass-count sentences are gone rather than renumbered' after an earlier commit (79ab97f) had deliberately reconciled three disagreeing counts — so the disagreement was reintroduced rather than removed. Confirmed by grepping every .md/src header for the counts.

The doc comment on the security-critical renderer still describes the rule that was deleted, contradicting both the implementation and docs/security.md. src/policy.ts:158 states displayProgram produces the 'basename of `argv[0]`, redacted with the audit rules (a program name CAN be credential-shaped …), capped so a pathological argument cannot flood the operator channel or the status block, and never blank'; the body performs no basename, never calls redactText, and REJECTS an over-long token instead of capping it (displayProgram(['a'.repeat(5000)]) === '(no command)'). src/host-runner.ts:65 repeats the same stale '(basename, redacted, capped, never blank)' description. Behavioural evidence that no redaction happens: displayProgram(['hunter2']) = 'hunter2', displayProgram(['Bearer']) = 'Bearer'. An auditor reading the function header (the natural entry point for this surface) is told there is a redaction step that does not exist.

AC-1's naming promise holds only for bare-word programs, narrower than stated. The sealed acceptance says `/devcontainer status` shows 'which PROGRAMS they named', and README.md:209 / README.zh-CN.md:147 repeat 'the programs they named' without qualification, but the single-branch rule renders every token carrying a separator as '(no command)'. Verified against the shipped ledger: noteFirstRun(['/usr/bin/docker']), noteFirstRun(['./build.sh']), noteFirstRun(['systemctl']) yields '3 host command attempts this session — most recent: (no command) | (no command) | systemctl'. The drift signal (the count, and the first-attempt notice) survives and docs/security.md:169-176 does disclose the '(no command)' outcome, so this is a wording/scope gap between the AC + README promise and the implemented rendering for path-spelled invocations (absolute paths and scripts — a normal way to call a host program), not a leak.

The d109ae1 renderer replacement left three documentation-of-record sites describing the OLD behaviour, so the code's own account of a security-relevant rendering contradicts the code. src/policy.ts:158 documents displayProgram as 'basename of argv[0], redacted with the audit rules (a program name CAN be credential-shaped - argv[0]="Authorization: Bearer sk-live-..." was reproduced by adversarial review), capped so a pathological argument cannot flood the operator channel'; src/host-runner.ts:65 documents it as '(basename, redacted, capped, never blank)'; extensions/index.ts:150 documents the one-shot notice as 'already redacted' (and its onFirstHostRun comment as 'an already REDACTED rendering'). The implementation does none of these: it takes the first whitespace-delimited token and whitelists ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._+-]{0,63}$, with no basename step and no redaction - the quoted 'Authorization: Bearer sk-live-...' example now renders '(no command)'. No runtime effect and the published docs (docs/security.md, CHANGELOG) are correct, but a maintainer reading these comments would believe an audit redaction rule is still in the path.

The new reverse guard makes every devcontainer_exec perform a SECOND full workspace discovery. In src/execution-service.ts a container-exec now calls options.mappingFor(ctx.workspaceKey) (the new guard, line ~190) and later options.resolveContainerWorkspace(ctx.workspaceKey) (the pre-existing presentation path, line ~288); in extensions/index.ts both are wired to functions that await the uncached registry(), which runs a host filesystem traversal plus 'docker ps --all --no-trunc' on every call (registry() has no memo), and readMapping is a near line-for-line duplicate of resolveContainerWorkspace. I confirmed with the real ExecutionService that one container-exec invokes both hooks exactly once each, so the change doubles a subprocess-spawning discovery per devcontainer_exec compared with the merge base (which performed one). It remains read-only and bounded, so AC-6 is not falsified, but the codebase elsewhere explicitly avoids discovering twice for one command and the two resolvers should share one read.

AC-4's 'binds exactly the picked candidate' fails when two candidates render the same picker label. chooseAmbiguousContainer builds labels as '<id.slice(0,12)> - <state>[ - <image>]' and maps the operator's answer back with labels.indexOf(picked), so two candidates whose ids share their first 12 characters (and whose state and image match) produce identical labels; the second row can never be bound. Confirmed by driving the real use handler: with candidates aaaaaaaaaaaa1111... and aaaaaaaaaaaa2222... (both running, same image), picking the second identical row bound candidate[0] and echoed 'Selected `/ws/project-a` -> container `aaaaaaaaaaaa1111...`'. It needs a 48-bit id-prefix collision, hence nit, but mapping a selection through a display string instead of the picker's index is the fragile part.

The published rendering contract omits the length bound the code enforces. docs/security.md ('a single word of [A-Za-z0-9._+-] starting with an alphanumeric') and the CHANGELOG bullet ('a single program word ([A-Za-z0-9._+-], leading alphanumeric)') state no cap, but the implementation's regex is ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._+-]{0,63}$, so displayProgram(['a'.repeat(65)]) renders '(no command)' and displayProgram(['a'.repeat(64)]) renders the word. Grepping docs, CHANGELOG and both READMEs finds the 64 ceiling nowhere, so the published specification claims a rendering the code refuses for a program-name-shaped token; AC-1 itself states the bound, so only the published docs are imprecise.

AC-1's stated tokenization is not what the implementation performs. The claim says displayProgram 'takes the first ASCII-whitespace-delimited token of argv[0]', but the implementation trims first with String.prototype.trim (Unicode-aware) and only then splits on [ \t\n\r\f\v]. Observed: displayProgram(['\u00A0docker']) returns 'docker', whereas dragging the AC's ASCII-whitespace rule over the raw argv[0] ('\u00A0docker' is one token, which fails the regex) yields '(no command)'. The divergence renders a program word the AC says would not render; it cannot expose anything outside [A-Za-z0-9._+-]{1,64}, so it is a specification/implementation mismatch rather than a leak.
